title: ～どころか — “far from ～ / let alone ～”
summary: Strongly denies what the listener expects (A) and gives something quite different or more extreme (B). Two uses: “far from A, rather the opposite B”, and “not even A, much less B”. It attaches to the plain form (な-adj: な / noun: without だ).

patterns.form: 普通形＋どころか、（むしろ）B
patterns.gloss: far from A, rather the opposite B

patterns.form: 名詞／数量＋どころか、Bさえ…ない
patterns.gloss: not even A, let alone B

body.p: かぜはよくなるどころか、もっとひどくなった: my cold didn’t get better, it got worse. A is what you would expect; B is the actual, opposite result. The speaker is often upset or surprised.
お金がないどころか、借金がある: not only no money, but debt. B is stronger than A in the same direction. Usually the sentence continues with Bも / Bさえ (にも, までも).
After どころか, a clause with the usual particles follows: 謝るどころか、逆に怒り出した. It is only for emphasis on contrast; not a polite expression and quite colloquial.

examples.ja: かぜは よくなる どころか、もっと ひどくなった。
examples.romaji: Kaze wa yokunaru dokoro ka, motto hidoku natta.
examples.tr: Far from getting better, my cold got worse.

examples.ja: 謝（あやま）るどころか、彼（かれ）は逆（ぎゃく）に怒（おこ）り出（だ）した。
examples.romaji: Ayamaru dokoro ka, kare wa gyaku ni okoridashita.
examples.tr: Far from apologizing, he got angry instead.

examples.ja: 楽（らく）になるどころか、仕事（しごと）はますます増（ふ）えた。
examples.romaji: Raku ni naru dokoro ka, shigoto wa masumasu fueta.
examples.tr: Far from getting easier, the work only kept increasing.

pitfalls: Don’t confuse どころか (denial + contrast) with どころではない (“no time for that”): different meaning.
な-adjectives take な (静かなどころか) and nouns take no だ (子どもどころか).
